name: Protestant Reformation
title: The story of the Protestant Reformation

text: More than 500 years ago, the Church of western Europe was one Church, led by the pope in Rome.
To raise money for a great church in Rome, preachers offered indulgences: the Church's promise of less punishment for sins.
src: At the beginning of the 16th century the Church of western and central Europe was a single institution under the pope in Rome
To raise money for the rebuilding of St Peter’s Basilica in Rome, Pope Leo X authorised a campaign of indulgence preaching / grants by the Church that remitted the temporal punishment still owed

text: Martin Luther, a friar who taught at the university of Wittenberg, wrote his Ninety-five Theses against the selling of indulgences.
Printed copies spread through Germany within weeks.
src: Martin Luther, an Augustinian friar and professor of theology at the university / 1517: Martin Luther writes his Ninety-five Theses against the sale of indulgences
Printed copies spread through Germany within weeks

text: Luther was called before the emperor Charles V at Worms, and he refused to take back his words.
A prince named Frederick the Wise hid him, and there Luther translated the New Testament into German.
src: he appeared that April before the emperor Charles V at the Diet of Worms and refused to recant
Frederick the Wise had him hidden in the Wartburg, where he translated the New Testament into German

text: Luther taught that people are saved by God's grace through faith alone, not by good works.
Other reformers, like Huldrych Zwingli of Zurich, shared these ideas but disagreed on others, and their churches grew apart.
src: sinners are made right with God by his grace, received through faith alone and not earned by good works
Other reformers shared these principles but differed on much else / In Zurich Huldrych Zwingli / the evangelical movement divided into Lutheran and Reformed branches

text: Many princes and cities took up the new teachings, and Protestant churches grew up beside the Catholic Church.
This split brought about a hundred years of wars between Catholics and Protestants, as in France.
src: Taken up or resisted by princes and cities / Lasting Protestant churches beside the Catholic Church
The division of Western Christianity brought a century of conflict / Catholics fought the Huguenots, as French Protestants were called

text: Today Protestant churches, such as the Lutheran, Anglican and Baptist churches, have hundreds of millions of members.
Its Bibles in everyday languages, such as the English King James Version, became great classics of those languages.
src: The Reformation left lasting churches that today count hundreds of millions of members: Lutheran, Reformed and Presbyterian, Anglican, Baptist and Mennonite
translations such as the Welsh Bible of 1588 and the King James Version of 1611 became classics of their languages
